function.name: search_google
function.description: Performs a search query on Google and returns a list of URLs that match the search criteria. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term to query on Google.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. The number must be a positive integer.

language.description: The language for the search results.

filter.description: A flag to filter explicit content in search results.

date_range.description: The date range for the search results in the format 'MM/DD/YYYY-MM/DD/YYYY'. If not specified, searches across all dates.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide to the most prominent vaccine manufacturers around the world.  It covers companies that have produced vaccines for COVID‑19, influenza, HPV, meningitis, and other diseases, and it highlights their most well‑known products and any unique manufacturing approaches.

| Region | Company | Headquarters | Notable Vaccines | Key Manufacturing Notes |
|--------|---------|--------------|------------------|--------------------------|
| **North America** | **Pfizer‑BioNTech** | New York, USA / Mainz, Germany | BNT162b2 (Comirnaty) – mRNA COVID‑19 vaccine | First large‑scale mRNA vaccine; uses lipid nanoparticle delivery; requires ultra‑cold chain (–70 °C). |
| | **Moderna** | Cambridge, USA | mRNA‑1273 (Spikevax) – COVID‑19 vaccine | mRNA platform; storage at 2–8 °C for 30 days (improved over Pfizer). |
| | **Johnson & Johnson (Janssen)** | New Brunswick, USA | Ad26.COV2.S – single‑dose adenovirus‑vector COVID‑19 vaccine | Adenoviral vector; stable at 2–8 °C; single dose. |
| | **Novavax** | Gaithersburg, USA | NVX-CoV2373 – protein subunit COVID‑19 vaccine | Recombinant spike protein + Matrix-M adjuvant; 2–8 °C. |
| | **Merck & Co.** | Kenilworth, USA | Gardasil 9 (HPV), RotaTeq (rotavirus) | Traditional recombinant subunit and live‑attenuated vaccines. |
| | **Sanofi Pasteur** | Lyon, France (global HQ) | Fluzone (influenza), Menactra (meningococcal) | Conventional egg‑based and cell‑culture influenza production. |
| | **GlaxoSmithKline (GSK)** | Brentford, UK | Shingrix (shingles), Fluzone Quadrivalent | Uses recombinant protein and adjuvants; cell‑culture influenza. |
| **Europe** | **AstraZeneca** | Cambridge, UK | ChAdOx1 nCoV‑19 (Vaxzevria) – adenovirus‑vector COVID‑19 vaccine | Uses chimpanzee adenovirus vector; 2–8 °C. |
| | **Bharat Biotech** | Hyderabad, India | Covaxin (BBV152) – inactivated COVID‑19 vaccine | Inactivated whole‑virus; 2–8 °C. |
| | **Sinovac Biotech** | Beijing, China | CoronaVac – inactivated COVID‑19 vaccine | Inactivated whole‑virus; 2–8 °C. |
| | **Sinopharm** | Beijing, China | BBIBP‑CorV – inactivated COVID‑19 vaccine | Inactivated whole‑virus; 2–8 °C. |
| | **CureVac** | Tübingen, Germany | CVnCoV – non‑replicating mRNA COVID‑19 vaccine | Non‑modified mRNA; 2–8 °C. |
| | **Biontech (German subsidiary of Pfizer)** | Mainz, Germany | BNT162b2 – mRNA COVID‑19 vaccine | Same as Pfizer‑BioNTech. |
| **Asia** | **Takeda Pharmaceutical** | Tokyo, Japan | Fluzone Quadrivalent, Shingrix | Cell‑culture influenza; recombinant subunit. |
| | **CureVac** | Tübingen, Germany (but active in Asia) | CVnCoV | Non‑modified mRNA. |
| | **Bharat Biotech** | Hyderabad, India | Covaxin | Inactivated. |
| | **Zydus Cadila** | Ahmedabad, India | Covaxin (in partnership) | Inactivated. |
| | **Serum Institute of India** | Pune, India | Covishield (AstraZeneca) | Adenovirus‑vector; 2–8 °C. |
| **Africa** | **Serum Institute of India** | Pune, India | Covishield | Distributed widely in Africa. |
| | **GSK** | Global | Shingrix, influenza | Distributed in many African countries. |
| **Australia** | **CSL Behring** | Melbourne, Australia | Influenza, hepatitis B | Cell‑culture influenza; recombinant subunit. |
| | **Sobi** | Stockholm, Sweden (but active in Australia) | Shingrix | Recombinant subunit. |

### How to Use This List

1. **Identify the Vaccine You’re Interested In**  
   - If you’re looking for a specific disease (e.g., COVID‑19, influenza, HPV), filter the table by the “Notable Vaccines” column.

2. **Check Storage Requirements**  
   - mRNA vaccines (Pfizer, Moderna, CureVac) often need cold‑chain logistics.  
   - Adenovirus‑vector and inactivated vaccines (AstraZeneca, J&J, Covaxin, CoronaVac) are more stable at 2–8 °C.

3. **Explore Manufacturing Platforms**  
   - **mRNA**: Lipid nanoparticles, synthetic RNA.  
   - **Adenovirus‑vector**: Replication‑defective viral vectors.  
   - **Inactivated**: Whole virus killed with formaldehyde or β‑propiolactone.  
   - **Recombinant protein**: Expressed in cell lines (CHO, HEK293, insect cells).  
   - **Live‑attenuated**: Weakened virus that can replicate minimally.

4. **Find More Details**  
   - For each company, you can visit their official website or look up their latest press releases.  
   - Regulatory filings (FDA, EMA, WHO) provide detailed product information and safety data.

---

#### Quick Links (clickable)

- **Pfizer‑BioNTech** – https://www.pfizer.com/
- **Moderna** – https://www.modernatx.com/
- **Johnson & Johnson (Janssen)** – https://www.jnj.com/
- **Novavax** – https://www.novavax.com/
- **AstraZeneca** – https://www.astrazeneca.com/
- **Bharat Biotech** – https://www.bharatbiotech.com/
- **Sinovac** – https://www.sinovac.com/
- **Sinopharm** – https://www.sinopharm.com/
- **Serum Institute of India** – https://www.serum.in/
- **GSK** – https://www.gsk.com/
- **Merck & Co.** – https://www.merck.com/
- **Sanofi Pasteur** – https://www.pasteur.org/
- **CureVac** – https://www.curevac.com/
- **CSL Behring** – https://www.cslbehring.com/

Feel free to let me know if you’d like deeper details on any particular manufacturer, vaccine platform, or regulatory status!
